div.div: 7 انزعج He was, or became, disquieted, disturbed, agitated, or flurried; (S, K;) and was, or became, removed, or unsettled, from his place: (S, A, L, Msb, K:) it may be thus used as quasipass. of ازعج: (Kh, Msb:) or it should not be so used: (Msb:) it is, however, agreeable with analogy, as is also ↓ ازدعج : (L:) but the word commonly used in its stead is شَخَصَ: (L, Msb:) زَعَجَ in this sense is not allowable. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
